name: Dibba Rotti
steps: Soak urad dal for 4 hours, drain and grind with some measured water to a thick fluffy paste. Rinse rice rava briefly and drain well.
Combine urad paste, rice rava, remaining water, salt, cumin, finely chopped chilli and ginger. Rest 30 minutes so the coarse rice hydrates; the batter should be thick enough to mound.
Heat half the oil in a heavy small pan. Spread half the batter into a thick 2–3 cm disc, cover and cook over very low heat for 12–15 minutes until the bottom forms a deep golden crust.
Drizzle a little oil over the top, flip carefully and cook uncovered for 8–10 minutes until the second side is crusty and the middle cooked. Repeat with the rest of the batter and oil.
Cut each thick rotti into wedges and serve warm with coconut chutney. The crisp outer crust and soft coarse-grained middle are essential.
tips: Do not rush the thick centre over high heat; it needs slow covered cooking.
passiveTime: Soak urad dal for 4 hours; rest the mixed batter for 30 minutes.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
